overview: This 446-page file traces Japan’s finances as the war in China expanded in 1937. Detailed 1937–38 budgets sit alongside diplomatic and Treasury assessments of military spending, bond financing, exchange controls, gold shipments, and foreign payments. Correspondence examines American bank credits, possible neutrality restrictions, and public opposition to financing Japan and Manchukuo.
interest: Detailed budget annexes reveal wartime borrowing; bank and diplomatic records show how officials assessed Japan’s financial limits.
